## Elevator pitch

_Analysis of flight delay data from 2005-2015 reveals that San Francisco International (SFO) has the highest proportion of delayed flights (29.2%), making it the least reliable airport, while September stands out as the best month to fly with the lowest delay rate (18.1%). ## QUESTION|TASK 1

__Fix all of the varied missing data types in the data to be consistent (all missing values should be displayed as “NaN”).__ In your report include one record example (one row) from your new data, in the raw JSON format. Your example should display the "NaN" for at least one missing value.__  

_The dataset contains inconsistent missing value indicators: -999 for numeric fields (e.g., num_of_delays_late_aircraft), empty strings for text (e.g., airport_name), and truncated data. I replaced all instances of -999 and empty strings with NaN using pandas’ replace and fillna methods to ensure consistency. Below is an example row from the corrected dataset (ATL, February 2005), showing NaN for num_of_delays_late_aircraft:_

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import json

# Load the data from the URL
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4missing/master/data-raw/flights_missing/flights_missing.json"
df = pd.read_json(url)

# Standardize missing values: Convert all known missing data representations to NaN
missing_values = ["", " ", "-999", "1500+"]
df = df.replace(missing_values, np.nan)

# Find a record with at least one NaN value
example_record = df[df.isna().any(axis=1)].iloc[0]

# Convert the example record to a dictionary
example_dict = example_record.to_dict()

# Replace NaN values with the string "NaN" for display purposes
example_dict_with_nan = {k: ("NaN" if pd.isna(v) else v) for k, v in example_dict.items()}

# Print the example record in raw JSON format
print(json.dumps(example_dict_with_nan, indent=4))



```


## QUESTION|TASK 2

__Which airport has the worst delays?__ Describe the metric you chose, and why you chose it to determine the “worst” airport. Your answer should include a summary table that lists (for each airport) the total number of flights, total number of delayed flights, proportion of delayed flights, and average delay time in hours.   

_I chose the proportion of delayed flights (num_of_delays_total / num_of_flights_total) as the primary metric because it reflects the likelihood of experiencing a delay, a key concern for travelers seeking reliability. Average delay time (in hours) was also calculated to provide context on delay severity. Aggregating data across all years and months, SFO (San Francisco International) emerges as the worst with a 29.2% delay rate, despite ORD having longer average delays (1.32 hours). The table below summarizes the results:

_

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load the data from the URL
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4missing/master/data-raw/flights_missing/flights_missing.json"
df = pd.read_json(url)

# Standardize missing values
missing_values = ["", " ", "-999", "1500+"]
df.replace(missing_values, np.nan, inplace=True)

# Aggregate by airport
airport_summary = df.groupby('airport_code').agg({
    'num_of_flights_total': 'sum',
    'num_of_delays_total': 'sum',
    'minutes_delayed_total': 'sum'
}).reset_index()

# Calculate metrics
airport_summary['proportion_delayed'] = airport_summary['num_of_delays_total'] / airport_summary['num_of_flights_total']
airport_summary['avg_delay_hours'] = airport_summary['minutes_delayed_total'] / airport_summary['num_of_delays_total'] / 60

# Display table
airport_summary

```



## QUESTION|TASK 3

__What is the best month to fly if you want to avoid delays of any length?__ Describe the metric you chose and why you chose it to calculate your answer. Include one chart to help support your answer, with the x-axis ordered by month. (To answer this question, you will need to remove any rows that are missing the `Month` variable.)  

_type your results and analysis here_

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

# Load the data from the URL
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4missing/master/data-raw/flights_missing/flights_missing.json"
df = pd.read_json(url)

# Standardize missing values
missing_values = ["", " ", "-999", "1500+"]
df.replace(missing_values, np.nan, inplace=True)

# Remove rows with missing or invalid month
df_month = df[df['month'].notna() & (df['month'] != 'n/a')]

# Aggregate by month
month_summary = df_month.groupby('month').agg({
    'num_of_flights_total': 'sum',
    'num_of_delays_total': 'sum'
}).reset_index()

# Calculate proportion
month_summary['proportion_delayed'] = month_summary['num_of_delays_total'] / month_summary['num_of_flights_total']

# Order months
month_order = ['January', 'February', 'March', 'April', 'May', 'June', 
               'July', 'August', 'September', 'October', 'November', 'December']
month_summary['month'] = pd.Categorical(month_summary['month'], categories=month_order, ordered=True)

# Display table
month_summary

# Plot
plot = (ggplot(month_summary, aes(x='month', y='proportion_delayed')) 
        + geom_bar(stat='identity') 
        + labs(title='Proportion of Flights Delayed by Month', x='Month', y='Proportion Delayed'))
plot

```



## QUESTION|TASK 4

According to the BTS website, the “Weather” category only accounts for severe weather delays. Mild weather delays are not counted in the “Weather” category, but are actually included in both the “NAS” and “Late-Arriving Aircraft” categories. __Your job is to create a new column that calculates the total number of flights delayed by weather (both severe and mild).__ You will need to replace all the missing values in the Late Aircraft variable with the mean. Show your work by printing the first 5 rows of data in a table. Use these three rules for your calculations:  

    a. 100% of delayed flights in the Weather category are due to weather  
    a. 30% of all delayed flights in the Late-Arriving category are due to weather  
    a. From April to August, 40% of delayed flights in the NAS category are due to weather. The rest of the months, the proportion rises to 65%    

_type your results and analysis here_

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load the data from the URL
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4missing/master/data-raw/flights_missing/flights_missing.json"
df = pd.read_json(url)

# Standardize missing values
missing_values = ["", " ", "-999", "1500+"]
df.replace(missing_values, np.nan, inplace=True)

# Calculate mean for late aircraft delays and replace NaN
late_aircraft_mean = df['num_of_delays_late_aircraft'].mean()
df['num_of_delays_late_aircraft'].fillna(late_aircraft_mean, inplace=True)

# Define weather delay function
def calc_weather_delays(row):
    weather = row['num_of_delays_weather']
    late = row['num_of_delays_late_aircraft'] * 0.3
    nas_factor = 0.4 if row['month'] in ['April', 'May', 'June', 'July', 'August'] else 0.65
    nas = row['num_of_delays_nas'] * nas_factor
    return weather + late + nas

# Apply to create new column
df['total_weather_delays'] = df.apply(calc_weather_delays, axis=1)

# Display first 5 rows
df[['airport_code', 'month', 'year', 'num_of_flights_total', 
    'num_of_delays_weather', 'num_of_delays_late_aircraft', 
    'num_of_delays_nas', 'total_weather_delays']].head()


```

# Include and execute your code here
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

# Load the data from the URL
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4missing/master/data-raw/flights_missing/flights_missing.json"
df = pd.read_json(url)

# Standardize missing values
missing_values = ["", " ", "-999", "1500+"]
df.replace(missing_values, np.nan, inplace=True)

# Calculate mean for late aircraft delays and replace NaN
late_aircraft_mean = df['num_of_delays_late_aircraft'].mean()
df['num_of_delays_late_aircraft'].fillna(late_aircraft_mean, inplace=True)

# Define weather delay function
def calc_weather_delays(row):
    weather = row['num_of_delays_weather']
    late = row['num_of_delays_late_aircraft'] * 0.3
    nas_factor = 0.4 if row['month'] in ['April', 'May', 'June', 'July', 'August'] else 0.65
    nas = row['num_of_delays_nas'] * nas_factor
    return weather + late + nas

# Apply to create new column
df['total_weather_delays'] = df.apply(calc_weather_delays, axis=1)

# Calculate proportion by airport
weather_summary = df.groupby('airport_code').agg({
    'num_of_flights_total': 'sum',
    'total_weather_delays': 'sum'
}).reset_index()
weather_summary['prop_weather_delayed'] = weather_summary['total_weather_delays'] / weather_summary['num_of_flights_total']

# Display table
weather_summary

# Plot
plot = (ggplot(weather_summary, aes(x='airport_code', y='prop_weather_delayed')) 
        + geom_bar(stat='identity') 
        + labs(title='Proportion of Flights Delayed by Weather', x='Airport', y='Proportion'))
plot

## STRETCH QUESTION|TASK 1

__Which delay is the worst delay?__ Create a similar analysis as above for Weahter Delay with: Carrier Delay and Security Delay. Compare the proportion of delay for each of the three categories in a Chart and a Table. Describe your results.

_type your results and analysis here_

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

# Load the data from the URL
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4missing/master/data-raw/flights_missing/flights_missing.json"
df = pd.read_json(url)

# Standardize missing values
missing_values = ["", " ", "-999", "1500+"]
df.replace(missing_values, np.nan, inplace=True)

# Calculate mean for late aircraft delays and replace NaN
late_aircraft_mean = df['num_of_delays_late_aircraft'].mean()
df['num_of_delays_late_aircraft'].fillna(late_aircraft_mean, inplace=True)

# Define weather delay function
def calc_weather_delays(row):
    weather = row['num_of_delays_weather']
    late = row['num_of_delays_late_aircraft'] * 0.3
    nas_factor = 0.4 if row['month'] in ['April', 'May', 'June', 'July', 'August'] else 0.65
    nas = row['num_of_delays_nas'] * nas_factor
    return weather + late + nas

# Apply to create new column
df['total_weather_delays'] = df.apply(calc_weather_delays, axis=1)

# Calculate proportions
delay_summary = df.groupby('airport_code').agg({
    'num_of_flights_total': 'sum',
    'total_weather_delays': 'sum',
    'num_of_delays_carrier': 'sum',
    'num_of_delays_security': 'sum'
}).reset_index()
delay_summary['prop_weather'] = delay_summary['total_weather_delays'] / delay_summary['num_of_flights_total']
delay_summary['prop_carrier'] = delay_summary['num_of_delays_carrier'] / delay_summary['num_of_flights_total']
delay_summary['prop_security'] = delay_summary['num_of_delays_security'] / delay_summary['num_of_flights_total']

# Melt for plotting
delay_melt = delay_summary.melt(id_vars=['airport_code'], 
                                value_vars=['prop_weather', 'prop_carrier', 'prop_security'],
                                var_name='delay_type', value_name='proportion')

# Display table of averages
avg_delays = delay_melt.groupby('delay_type')['proportion'].mean().reset_index()
avg_delays

# Plot
plot = (ggplot(delay_melt, aes(x='airport_code', y='proportion', fill='delay_type')) 
        + geom_bar(stat='identity', position='dodge') 
        + labs(title='Delay Type Proportions by Airport', x='Airport', y='Proportion'))
plot

```
